name: Research, compare and recommend a product
user_input: Research three open-source text-to-speech tools, compare their licence and language support, and write a one-paragraph recommendation for a student project.

expected_plan.notes: Comparison requires at least three retrieved sources; the recommendation step must depend on the extraction step.

expected_output_criteria: At least three distinct tools are named in the comparison.
Each named tool has a licence and a language-support statement.
Every factual claim is attributed to a retrieved source.
failure_conditions: Fewer than three tools are compared.
The recommendation is produced before the comparison is complete.
A factual claim about a tool is not supported by any retrieved passage.

evaluation_criteria.task_completion: Run reaches the success terminal state with a comparison and a recommendation.
evaluation_criteria.planning_quality: Plan schema valid; the recommendation step declares a dependency on the comparison step.
evaluation_criteria.tool_selection_accuracy: web.search, web.fetch and llm.extract are each selected at least once; no unrelated tool is invoked.
evaluation_criteria.verification_accuracy: Verification confirms three distinct tools were compared and that a recommendation exists; the human label confirms both.
evaluation_criteria.recovery_effectiveness: Not applicable: no failure is injected in the base run. Recorded as null, not zero.
evaluation_criteria.evidence_accuracy: At least 80% of cited evidence spans support the claim they are attached to.
evaluation_criteria.execution_time: Wall-clock time from goal intake to terminal state is recorded. No pass/fail threshold applies; execution time is a trade-off metric, reported alongside task completion.

adversarial_notes: This scenario favours condition C, since it needs retrieval plus comparison plus verification. It is also the scenario where an LLM-only baseline (condition B) is most likely to produce a fluent recommendation with fabricated licence claims, so a large B-to-C gap here is expected and should be reported as a mechanism, not generalised as a universal effect. Note that condition C can also fail here by over-fragmenting the plan into too many steps or by exhausting its retry budget on flaky network fetches.
